They annihilate the displayed holomorphic coordinates and, together with $\partial_{\bar t}$, form a direct local frame of $T^{0,1}Z$. $0\le i\le r$. For nonempty $I\subseteq\{0,\ldots,r\}$ write
$U_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$. For $r\ge1$ and $k\in\mathbb Z$, let
$\mathcal O(k)$ be the line bundle with local frames satisfying
$e_j^{(k)}=(Z_j/Z_i)^k e_i^{(k)}$ on $U_i\cap U_j$; write
$\mathcal O=\mathcal O(0)$ and $\mathbb C^*=\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$. Analytic
sheaf cohomology $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is the $q$th right-derived
global-sections group of the abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$. For this ordered cover
and a sheaf $\mathcal G$, define
$$C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=\prod_{|I|=p+1}\mathcal G(U_I),\qquad (\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{p+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{p+1}}|_{U_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}}},$$
for $0\le p\le r$, with $C^p=0$ otherwise and increasing indices;
fixed-cover Čech cohomology is the cohomology of this complex. A mixed
Laurent–Taylor series is **normally convergent** when it
converges absolutely and uniformly on every compact product subset of its
domain. For $r\ge1$, every
$U_I$ is biholomorphic to
$\mathbb C^{r+1-|I|}\times(\mathbb C^*)^{|I|-1}$. For every integer $k$,
each section on $U_I$, in a standard local frame, has a unique normally
convergent mixed Laurent–Taylor expansion indexed by exponent tuples
$m=(m_0,\ldots,m_r)\in\mathbb Z^{r+1}$ with $\sum_i m_i=k$; its coefficient
occurs on $U_I$ exactly when $N(m):=\{i:m_i<0\}\subseteq I$. Restrictions
preserve each coefficient. In the ordered-cover Čech complex, every mode with
nonempty proper $N(m)$ has the cochain contraction, for $c\in C^p$ and an
output index $I$ of size $p$, given by $(h_mc)_I=0$ if $j\in I$ and
$(h_mc)_I=(-1)^{\#\{i\in I:i<j\}}c_{I\cup\{j\}}$ if $j\notin I$, where

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

On a form annihilating vertical tangent, the mixed component is the intrinsic vertical Bott/Dolbeault operator on the horizontal coefficient bundle: it is obtained by evaluating $\bar\partial$ on one vertical and one horizontal vector. This description is independent of the lift of the horizontal vector. In the constant-$t$ local frame the vectors $\partial_{\bar t},H_1,H_2$ commute; hence that coefficient operator is ordinary $\partial_{\bar t}$.

Let $Q_x\subset\mathbb C^4$ be the quaternionic two-plane over $x$. Its Hermitian quaternionic structure gives a canonical complex alternating volume form $\delta_x$: every frame $(v,jv)$ of unit norm has determinant one for this form, and the changes are in $SU(2)$. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Its holomorphic-section space is zero by the fibre calculation in [F2], so the horizontal form vanishes; the original class is exact and is therefore zero. Thus the global map is injective.
